slides.reasoning: Design A delivers the specified condensed futurist numerals, a dramatic full-bleed rising curve and a tightly ruled metric stack, while Design B leaves large dead zones, uses off-brand blue/red point markers, and defaults to generic chart styling.

Design A builds a genuine hand-drawn illustrated route with clay/marigold/aubergine used across a layered composition, whereas Design B is a sparse centered timeline with a stray tilted red block and large unbalanced empty areas.

Design A shows a precise enterprise before/after with sharp rules, a clear ROI band and disciplined margins; Design B's flowchart boxes and floating dots with crossing leader lines read as clip-art and the diagram's spatial logic collapses.

Design A's orbital allocation wheel, gold serif hierarchy and ruled construction table feel institutional, though its '20%' label slightly kisses the ring; Design B is a plain donut plus a redundant legend with large unused space at bottom right.

Design A makes the product hero with brushed-silver staging, annotated callouts and a crisp spec ledger, while Design B's dark photo fights the specified silver-dominant palette, obscures the product and pastes an awkward fake 'ARC ONE' label onto it.

Design A is a coherent monospaced navy scorecard with one performance curve, variance markers and an emphatic activation gap bar; Design B collides 'ACTIVATION' with 'TARGET 75%' and misuses a single line to connect unrelated regional and activation metrics.

Design A delivers a true custom transit-line diagram with wayfinding typography and a strong charcoal measures bar, while Design B reduces the pillars to four bar strips plus an unexplained black 'NORTH STAR' circle amid loose whitespace.

Design A's phase bands scaled to a week ruler, diamond gates and team dot-counts read as a real program roadmap; Design B uses equal-height blocks unrelated to duration and leaves a wide empty band above the footer.

Design A renders an actual closed loop with marker-style annotations, a worked example panel and a highlighted practice rule, whereas Design B's diamond of circles has cramped text inside the discs and an orphaned 'PRACTICE RULE' rule with a large empty lower half.

Design A's oversized editorial 68%, dot-matrix proof and annotated three-app handover chain are far more memorable and better spaced than Design B's plain donut and pill-and-arrow row with a wide empty right margin.

Design A's layered oversized headline, visible/hidden UI diagram and boxed provocation create a keynote moment on brand cobalt; Design B's stock audience photo dilutes the concept and its stacked white/black label blocks feel like a default template.

Design A balances four oversized metrics with tags, a customer-voice card and a ranked 90-day list under a confident closing bar, while Design B scatters metrics unevenly, leaves large orange voids and lets the closing line float without structure.

Design A's illustrated corridor map with km markers, scale bar and a field-journal info column is both emotional and informational; Design B overlays crude orange bars on a mismatched tropical karst photo that contradicts the Karri-to-coast narrative.

Design A's huge letterform sits on a real baseline grid with clean leader lines and definitions plus a Bauhaus color chip, while Design B's labels are disconnected rules floating away from the glyph, with 'BOWL' and 'COUNTER' pointing to empty space.

Design A is a genuine collage with ingredient-macro graphic forms, a segmented audience bar and a plum/peach footer that avoids a pricing table; Design B's photo panel is generic and its bottom-right email sits nearly illegibly over the image edge.
